title: Philippines, France conduct bilateral maritime exercise
summary: The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) through its Naval Command Western Mindanao (NCWM), Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) and the French Armed Forces conducted their 3rd Bilateral Maritime…

blocks.text: The BMCA was conducted under the area of responsibility of the Western Mindanao Command, said NCWM commander Rear Adm. Constancio Arturo Reyes Jr.
Armed Forces of the Philippines / Facebook page

MANILA, Philippines — The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) through its Naval Command Western Mindanao (NCWM), Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) and the French Armed Forces conducted their 3rd Bilateral Maritime Cooperative Activity (BMCA) in the Sulu Sea, reinforcing maritime interoperability and defense cooperation between the two forces.

The Philippines deployed the Philippine Navy’s BRP Diego Silang, supported by its AW109 helicopter and other air assets from the Philippine Air Force, such as the C-208B and S-70i Blackhawk helicopters, along with the PCG’s BRP Sarangani during the MCA from Nov. 20 to 22.

France participated with the Floréal-class frigate, the FS Vendémiaire, and a French Navy AS365 Dauphin helicopter, demonstrating the two countries’ shared commitment to strengthening maritime security and cooperation.

“The successful conduct of the 3rd Philippines-France BMCA demonstrated the growing operational cooperation between the two countries and their ability to work together in addressing shared maritime security challenges,” Reyes said.

The AFP said the three-day activity featured communications exercises, personnel exchanges, cross-deck vertical replenishment, division tactics and officer-of-the-watch maneuvers, photo exercise and the cross Visit, Board, Search, and Seizure exercise.

According to the AFP, the activity underscores the “growing defense partnership between the Philippines and France and their shared commitment to a secure, stable, and rules-based maritime environment.”
Meanwhile, the AFP tested its air and missile defense capabilities during a joint military exercise in Northern Luzon as part of the 10-day AFP Joint Exercise DAGIT-PA.

The AFP conducted an integrated air and missile defense exercise on Nov. 19 at Camp Cape Bojeador in Burgos, Ilocos Norte, testing its ability to detect, track and intercept simulated airborne threats through coordinated operations involving joint air and surface assets.
The 10-day exercise from Nov. 17 to 27 covers various operational areas in Northern Luzon and Palawan.

The DAGIT-PA – which stands for dagat, langit, lupa (sea, air, land) – brings together the Philippine Army, Philippine Air Force, Philippine Navy and Philippine Marine Corps to enhance interoperability and coordination in joint land, air, and maritime operations.
It also integrates the Reserve Force in joint and combined missions, reinforcing unity of effort and the AFP’s ability to respond to evolving security challenges. — Roel Pareño
